title: Talk Is Cheap, Show Me Your Colors: Low-Budget Consistency Auditing for Aggregated LLM Services

creators.name: He, Xiguan
creators.affiliation: College of Information, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine

creators.name: Li, Siqi
creators.affiliation: College of Information, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine

description:
Aggregated large language model (LLM) services expose declared model identifiers while hiding the backend configurations fulfilling client requests. We present HuePrint, a black-box framework that audits brokered endpoint consistency via structured color elicitation (#RRGGBB and R,G,B) and continuous geometric distribution comparison without model weights or token probabilities.

Across 38,688 deduplicated live cloud responses spanning 56 endpoints and 12 backends (Datasets A–E and Studies S1–S5), HuePrint lowers 30-call/side equal error rates over single-word baselines from 4.52–5.23% to 0.94–1.00% on our development cohort and from 6.25–8.04% to 3.49–5.00% across 20 locked endpoints, reaching 0.00% at 60–150 calls/side. In a same-day 20-model parity benchmark (Study S5), 30-call/side HuePrint averages 3.48% all-pairs (range 1.32–5.00%) and 5.18% within-family equal error rates (range 0.00–7.89%; matched split 1.32% / 0.00%) across all ten balanced 3v3 splits at $0.0068 query cost, outperforming open-set LLMmap (10.53–34.39% within-family across 1–3 traces, 95% safety refusal on q1) and cost-matched long-form continuation kernels (11.09–19.47%), while scoring traces over 15,000 times faster locally (0.08–0.31 ms vs. 4,701.9 ms). Regularized RGB energy halves shallow-census error relative to exact-hex divergence (5.36% vs. 10.71%), and a multi-scale hybrid cuts cross-provider error across 12 hosts from 16.67% to 5.93%. Across 21-day cross-gateway transfers, same- and different-label pairs remain fully separated by score (0.00% EER) and every rule catches 182/182 swaps: budget-matched B6v6 frozen thresholds flag 1/14 raw (0/14 self-centered) same-label pairs, while stratified energy permutation testing rejects distribution equality for 6/14 of the same pairs. Unified Lipschitz bounds and estimator diagnostics guide calibration: self-centering cuts held-out false rejections from 30% to 10%, U-statistic ratios remove bootstrap enrollment, private prompt-pool subsampling cuts per-cell reuse 4.0×, and in offline replay two-stage confirmation reduces false alerts from 14 to 1 across 100 same-label S3 windows while flagging 186/190 within-family substitution windows under $0.01 expected cost.

Version 2.1.0 changes: Added same-day competitor benchmark Study S5 (4,160 calls across LLMmap, Gao et al. long-form continuation MMD, and HuePrint; 38,688 cloud responses total across 15 frozen JSONL logs), offline operational defenses (private prompt-pool subsampling, two-stage sequential cascade, Study S2 side-channel decontamination, external U-statistic verification, and all-10 balanced S5c partitions), updated 12-page IEEE Computer Society main manuscript, and expanded 20-page Supplementary Material.

This Zenodo record includes the complete preprint with supplementary material (HuePrint_Preprint.pdf, 32 pages), standalone main (12 pages) and supplementary (20 pages) PDFs, and a self-contained offline replication package (HuePrint_Replication_Package.zip) containing all 15 read-only JSONL response corpora, multilingual prompt batteries, statistical analysis scripts, unit tests, and SHA-256 integrity manifests (58 baseline plus 10 Study S5 locked files).
